findings.subject: chat-typing-indicator
findings.summary: ChatTypingIndicator's announcement is unreliable and suppressed in its documented usage, and its dots vanish under forced colors.
findings.evidence: chat-typing-indicator.tsx:22-28 mounts role=status with only aria-label and no text, so there is no content change to announce; every documented placement nests it in ChatMessage streaming, which sets aria-busy=true (chat-message.tsx:69; chat-typing-indicator.stories.tsx:22-24; packages/templates/src/blocks/chat-panel/chat-panel.tsx:131-146; apps/docs/src/pages/pattern-agent.mdx:67-82); dots are background-color: currentColor only (chat-typing-indicator.css:22) with no forced-colors rule (grep forced-colors in components/chat-*: none).
findings.fix: Render the label as visually hidden text inside the status (not aria-label), and document or enforce that the status sits outside any aria-busy ancestor (or have ChatMessage not set aria-busy while it holds only the indicator). Add @media (forced-colors: active) { .a63-ChatTypingIndicator-dot { background-color: CanvasText; forced-color-adjust: none } } or draw the dots with a border. Add a test for the in-message placement.

verified.reason: Reproduced from source. chat-typing-indicator.tsx:22-37 renders role=status whose only children are aria-hidden dots, so the live region has no text content; its name comes only from aria-label. A live region that mounts already filled, with nothing changing inside it afterwards, is not reliably announced, so the comment at lines 12-14 ('announces it once') overstates what happens. Every documented usage nests it in ChatMessage with streaming: chat-message.tsx:69 sets aria-busy={streaming}. The InMessage story (stories.tsx:22-24), ChatPanel's assistant message (chat-panel.tsx:131 sets streaming, the indicator is at :145-146) and the docs pattern (pattern-agent.mdx ~66-80, getMessageText(message) || <ChatTypingIndicator/> inside ChatMessage streaming) all do this. aria-busy on an ancestor lets assistive technology hold back changes until the busy state ends, which makes the announcement even less likely. Forced colors: chat-typing-indicator.css:22 paints the dots with background-color: currentColor. Forced-colors mode replaces background-color with Canvas, the dots have no border or outline, and grep finds no forced-colors rule in components/chat-*. In that mode the component's only visible content disappears. Both are K2 gaps: wrong role/name behaviour and forced colors. The 'ready' blocker is the vanishing dots, so P1 stands rather than P0, because the message still arrives as text afterwards.

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: Sending with the send button strands keyboard focus on a now-disabled button, and the footnote is not described to the field.
findings.evidence: chat-composer.tsx:150-154 clears the own value after send; tsx:240 disabled={!canSend} then disables the focused button. Footnote at tsx:252-256 has no id/aria-describedby link to the textarea.
findings.fix: After a button-initiated send, return focus to the textarea (or keep the button focusable with aria-disabled); give the footnote an id and set aria-describedby on the field.

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: ChatComposer has no phone story; its keyboard and safe-area behaviour at phone width is uncaptured.
findings.evidence: chat-composer.stories.tsx:22-27 fixes the decorator at 640px and no story sets a phone viewport; only templates-blocks-chat-panel-phone-chromium-linux.png shows it at 390px; field cap is max-height: 40vh (chat-composer.css:43).
findings.fix: Add a Phone story (AppView layout=phone or a 390px viewport, coarse pointer) with a baseline, and cap the field with dvh/svh.

findings.subject: chat-message
findings.summary: Chat bubbles and Message bubbles are fill-only with no forced-colors treatment, so they lose shape and direction in forced colors.
findings.evidence: chat-message.css:64-68 and message.css:66-74 draw bubbles with background-color only; no forced-colors rule in components/chat-* or message (grep). Applies to chat-message and message.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors rule giving bubbles a 1px CanvasText border (or a transparent border at rest that forced colors makes visible).

findings.subject: message
findings.summary: Message bubble overflow:hidden clips the focus outline of links or buttons inside it, and its bubbles also lack forced-colors treatment (see r1-k09-chat-4).
findings.evidence: message.css:61 overflow:hidden on .a63-Message-bubble; contract guidance says content can be a link (message.tsx:66-68).
findings.fix: Clip only the media (overflow on .a63-Message-media with inherited radii) or inset focus outlines inside the bubble with negative outline-offset.

findings.subject: chat-message
findings.summary: ChatMessage has no designed error/failed-turn state and no visual for streaming; hosts hand-roll the error.
findings.evidence: Contract states rest, streaming only (`atom63 component chat-message`); pattern-agent.mdx:71-79 builds the error with a text-destructive span and a Retry Button; data-streaming (chat-message.tsx:75) is unstyled in chat-message.css.
findings.fix: Add an error state (contract + recipe: danger text/icon and an actions-slot retry convention) with a story and baseline; decide whether streaming needs a visual cue.

findings.subject: message
findings.summary: Delivered and read are visually identical, and failed has no danger cue or retry affordance.
findings.evidence: message.tsx:35-37 maps delivered and read to the same CheckCheck icon; message.css has no data-status styling; ui-react-message-delivery-states-chromium-linux.png shows identical delivered/read rows and a failed row in the normal bubble foreground.
findings.fix: Distinguish read (e.g. accent-tinted or filled ticks via a --a63-message-status-read token) and give failed a danger-coloured icon plus a documented retry slot or pattern.

findings.subject: message
findings.summary: The Message Themes baseline bypasses ThemeMatrix, so retro and terminal render with modern rounded bubbles and the archetype is misrepresented.
findings.evidence: message.stories.tsx:161-180 uses UIProvider directly; story-probes.tsx:80-131 documents that per-theme radius needs the ThemeMatrix ramp; ui-react-message-themes-chromium-linux.png retro/terminal bubbles are pill-shaped while ui-react-chatmessage-themes-chromium-linux.png is square in the same themes.
findings.fix: Render the Themes story through ThemeMatrix (as the other four chat components do) and re-baseline; YZ then judges the retro/terminal bubble look.

findings.subject: chat-steps
findings.summary: The ChatSteps trigger is a 32px target on coarse pointers, with no 44px hit area.
findings.evidence: chat-steps.css:25 min-block-size: var(--a63-control-min-size); environment.css:45-55 defines min-size (rendered floor) vs min-target (44px touch); no hit-area pseudo, unlike button.css:630-640.
findings.fix: Expand the trigger's interactive area to --a63-control-min-target (hit-area pseudo-element, as Button does).

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: Inline-to-block switching only re-measures on typing, so a host-set value or a resize leaves the layout stale.
findings.evidence: chat-composer.tsx:139-143 and 178-185: wrappedAt is set only inside onChange via wraps().
findings.fix: Measure in a layout effect keyed on value and on a ResizeObserver of the field.
